hook.text: Milgrain is a border of tiny beads.

lines.text: Milgrain is a border of tiny beads.
The beads run along an edge or around a stone.
They frame the stone and draw the eye to it.
The old way was to solder each bead on by hand.
The faster way is a small tool with a toothed wheel.
Rolled along the edge, it raises beads from the metal itself.
Wheels come in numbered sizes, and bigger numbers make bigger beads.
Today many pieces are designed in 3D and cast.
lines.say: Today many pieces are designed in three D and cast.

lines.text: It is most linked with platinum and the early 1900s.
lines.say: It is most linked with platinum and the early nineteen hundreds.

lines.text: The name is French for a thousand grains.
So milgrain is a line of tiny beads framing a stone.
A render shows the border and the stone before anything is cast.

post.caption: Milgrain is a border of tiny metal beads along the edge of a band or around a stone. It frames the stone and draws the eye to it. The old way was to solder one bead at a time by hand, and the faster way is a small tool with a toothed wheel that raises the beads from the metal itself. Milgrain is most linked with platinum and the early 1900s, and the name is French for a thousand grains. The renders in this video were made with HeyGema.
